title: Farewell to Gacha-Style AI Video! MAGI-2 Launches with 50ms-Level Precise Camera Control, Reshaping Video Industrialization Standards at ¥0.5/Second
excerpt: In the field of AI video generation, creators have long been trapped in the anxiety of “opening a blind box”: image details are uncontrollable, shot transitions
content_html:
In the field of AI video generation, creators have long been trapped in the anxiety of “opening a blind box”: image details are uncontrollable, shot transitions depend on luck, and high trial-and-error costs make commercial deployment extremely difficult. As the industry struggles with the toy-like dilemma of being “watchable but unusable,” a revolution aimed at reshaping the industrialization standards of AI video has arrived.

Recently, Sand AI officially released its next-generation video generation model, MAGI-2. With a total parameter count of 480B, this model not only ranks second globally on the Artificial Analysis video generation leaderboard, but also stuns the market with an extreme price of RMB 0.5 per second for 1080P video—only 1/10 that of mainstream models of the same specification—declaring that AI video is moving from “random gacha pulls” to “precise industrial-scale production.”

50-millisecond-level precise shot control: ending the industry’s chronic problem of “instruction failure”

MAGI-2’s biggest breakthrough is that it truly returns control over video generation to creators. The model supports prompts of up to 20,000 characters and can accurately parse subjects, positions, action sequences, and timing of appearance.

Even more impressive is its “50-millisecond-level” shot-cut control. Creators can precisely specify instructions such as “turn the head and accelerate at second 03” or “leap over the stall at second 06,” with measured average time deviation of no more than 0.1 seconds. With mixed input of up to 20 reference assets per generation (10 images + 5 videos + 5 audio clips), the model can perfectly reproduce the color palette, brushstrokes, and texture in reference images, allowing complex commercial storyboard scripts to be realized at pixel-level precision.

Emergent intelligence: from “passive execution” to “autonomous directing”

With the leap in parameter scale and training data (expanded by about 3x), MAGI-2 demonstrates surprising “emergent intelligence.” Without prompt enhancement (PE) enabled, the model does not rely on external language model assistance and can independently complete complex logical reasoning and narrative planning.

For example, when given an image of a 9×9 Sudoku puzzle, the model can use image-to-video (I2V) to autonomously reason through the solving steps and dynamically demonstrate them. In narrative scenes, by inputting only staged plot beats such as “Lu Su boards the boat and takes a seat,” “the two converse,” and “Kongming reveals his purpose,” the model can autonomously arrange shot sizes, camera angles, and cut timing to generate a coherent dialogue scene with a cinematic feel. This leap from “image generator” to “autonomous director” greatly lowers the barrier to professional video creation.

Technical foundation: deep coupling of MoE architecture and domestic computing power

What supports such massive capability is a comprehensive evolution of the underlying architecture. MAGI-2 adopts an innovative Multi-Head Latent MoE architecture, dividing the latent space into multiple independent subspaces for expert routing. With self-developed technologies such as Head Parallel and MagiFSDP, it achieved about 22% training acceleration in 480B pretraining comparison experiments, effectively controlling computation and communication overhead.

It is worth mentioning that MAGI-2 has fully completed adaptation to domestic chips such as Hygon and Moore Threads. In an era when computing supply chains are increasingly important, this not only broadens the model’s deployment options, but also provides a solid foundation for domestic enterprises to develop large-model applications based on domestic computing power.

The last piece of the puzzle on the road to perfection

Despite its significant leap in capability, the MAGI-2 team remains clear-headed and restrained. The official team openly admits that the model still has room for continuous optimization in image stability during high-speed motion scenes, the jerkiness of mid-to-long-shot 2D animation, and the richness of audio and sound effect layers. This honesty about technical boundaries is precisely the mark of a mature industrial-grade product.

Currently, MAGI-2’s API service is open for applications from strategic partner customers, and individual creators can be among the first to experience it through LibTV. When a cost of RMB 0.5 per second meets 50-millisecond-level precise control, the “iPhone moment” of AI video generation may have already arrived. In future video creation, what matters will no longer be who has the greater computing power, but who can use the lowest trial-and-error cost to translate imagination into reality with the greatest precision.
